text:
The Senators are 15-6-3, with points in eight straight (6-0-2), and this one doesn't need an asterisk. Ottawa has won 59% of the expected goals during the run (expected goals measure the quality of chances) and 53% on the season, its goals almost exactly match its chances, and our playoff odds sit at 91% with a 23% shot at the Atlantic.

The depth is what stands out. Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Ridly Greig have allowed chances at a rate of 0.69 expected goals per 60 at 5v5, which is about as stingy as a line gets, and they win 81% of the expected goals. Tim Stützle's line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund (66%) and Shane Pinto's group with Drake Batherson and Philip Tomasino (61%) are both well above water. Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have been on for 17 goals for and 8 against at 5v5.

The week had its human side, too. Nick Cousins returned from a concussion after Jakob Chychrun's hit, telling RMNB he holds no hard feelings ("I've never been hit that hard before"), and Tyler Boucher, Brian Boucher's son, made his NHL debut.

And the front office is shopping. Elliotte Friedman reported Senators interest in Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, with general manager Steve Staios scouting the Penguins in Nashville on Saturday. The one worry, raised on the Sens Nation Podcast, is the return of backup goalie concerns behind Linus Ullmark.
